dataflow.outcome: wrong-recipient disclosure of declared embedding secret and document/query text
dataflow.sink: API-key-authenticated Gemini/effective-base model discovery and embedding request
dataflow.source: operator-controlled embedding declaration and text selected for embedding
dataflow.summary: `tools.toml` embedding fields -> `declared_adapter_for_role()` -> registered `DeclaredAdapter` with only model/auth -> `active_adopted_embedding_execution()` -> `run_adopted_embedding()` -> `GeminiEmbeddingAdapter::default()` -> `EnvGeminiEmbeddingClient::embed()`

impact.why: The recipient can receive a declared embedding credential and indexed document or query text.

likelihood.why: The path requires local configuration and online execution gates, but the dispatch is deterministic once those preconditions hold.

limitations: This path does not directly execute code on the local host.
Aligned official Gemini declarations or an intentionally aligned base URL may avoid practical recipient drift.

reachability.entrypoint: accepted embedding adapter declaration plus later embedding operation
reachability.outcome: the effective recipient receives an API key and text outside the declared provider/model boundary
reachability.summary: Local operator configuration, a resolvable credential, general online opt-in, budget availability, and an embedding invocation are required.

attackPath.summary: A KCS operator accepts or supplies a non-Gemini/private/offline/different-model embedding declaration with an auth reference. Later, online embedding executes through the fixed Gemini/effective-base client, which attaches the retained credential and sends eligible text to a recipient not bound to the accepted declaration.

category: adapter destination/model confusion and wrong-recipient credential/text disclosure

codeEvidence.explanation: The schema accepts the fields that identify an embedding adapter execution target, model, and credential reference.
codeEvidence.label: Embedding declarations accept destination and model fields

codeEvidence.explanation: After validation, the runtime declaration has no field for `kind`, `cmd`, `args`, or `url`, so the accepted recipient identity is no longer available to the executor.
codeEvidence.label: Runtime projection keeps only model and auth

codeEvidence.explanation: The conversion preserves the credential reference but drops the declared destination fields before registration.
codeEvidence.label: Conversion copies model/auth but not URL or kind

codeEvidence.explanation: A declared embedding credential is enough to activate the real path; no declared destination or model comparison remains in this decision.
codeEvidence.label: Declared auth selects real embedding execution

codeEvidence.explanation: The real branch does not dispatch the accepted adapter; it always constructs the default Gemini embedding adapter.
codeEvidence.label: Real execution dispatches the default Gemini adapter

codeEvidence.explanation: The effective HTTP base is a programmatic value, `GEMINI_API_BASE`, or Google default, while the credential comes from the embedding role declaration or legacy environment fallback.
codeEvidence.label: Gemini client derives its own base and resolves the embedding credential

codeEvidence.explanation: The sink attaches the retained secret and serializes each embedding item text into the request sent to the effective Gemini base.
codeEvidence.label: Embedding text and API key are sent to the effective Gemini base

codeEvidence.explanation: The user-facing gate confirms generic network and embedding behavior, but it does not reveal or enforce equality between the declared provider/model and the effective Gemini recipient.
codeEvidence.label: Preview describes generic online embedding rather than recipient binding

invariants: Accepted embedding destination/model must equal the effective request destination/model.
Custom-provider credentials must not be attached to the built-in Gemini endpoint.
Ambient `GEMINI_API_BASE` must not silently override a declaration-bound destination.
remediation.summary: Reject unsupported embedding targets or preserve and dispatch the exact accepted provider/model identity. Bind approval, credential resolution, runtime dispatch, and provenance to the same adapter identity.
tests: A non-Gemini `[embedding]` declaration with `url`, `model`, and `auth` is rejected unless a matching implementation exists.
If custom embedding is supported, the request base URL and model are exactly the declared URL and model.
Preview and approval output fails or warns when declared and effective provider/model differ.

rootCause.summary: The violated invariant is that an embedding credential and text should be sent only to the provider/model identity accepted for the embedding role. KCS accepts destination fields, then projects them out of `DeclaredAdapter`; the remaining `auth` field activates real execution, and the real branch always dispatches the fixed Gemini adapter.

summary: KCS accepts embedding declarations with target, command/URL, model, and auth fields, but the runtime DeclaredAdapter keeps only model/auth. A declared embedding auth reference activates real execution, and the real branch always dispatches GeminiEmbeddingAdapter::default(), so the retained secret and embedding text can be sent to the fixed Gemini/effective-base recipient instead of the accepted provider/model.
title: Accepted embedding adapter targets are discarded before fixed Gemini execution

assertions: A retained declared auth reference activates `AdoptedEmbeddingExecution::Real`.
The Gemini client attaches the resolved embedding API key and item text to the effective Gemini request.
limitations: No live embedding request or loopback capture was performed.
The prevalence of non-Gemini embedding declarations in deployed configurations was not measured.
validation.method: static source trace plus local non-network regression probe
validation.summary: The saved V10 validation and local PoC confirm the source path from accepted embedding declaration fields, through lossy projection and auth-triggered real execution, to the fixed Gemini authenticated text sink.
